# Rollout Plan: Migrating 40,000 Users from Legacy Billing to New Billing System

## Overview

Both billing systems will run in parallel throughout the migration, allowing gradual cutover with a fast rollback path at every stage. Users remain fully billable at all times — no user is ever left in a state where neither system is authoritative for them. The old system stays fully operational and unmodified in scope through the entire migration; its retirement is explicitly out of scope for this plan and must be a separate, later initiative.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (5% of users — 2,000 users)

**Target:** Internal accounts, employee accounts, and opted-in low-risk customers (e.g., month-to-month plans, no active disputes, no complex proration/credits history).

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed full parallel-run reconciliation against the old system for at least 14 consecutive days on synthetic/shadow traffic with zero unexplained discrepancies, and rollback tooling (re-pointing a migrated account back to the old system) has been tested end-to-end in staging.

**Duration:** 2 weeks minimum before proceeding.

**Activities:** Migrate accounts, run dual invoicing in shadow mode (new system generates invoices but old system's invoice remains the source of truth sent to the customer), compare line-by-line output daily.

---

## Phase 2: Early Majority (30% of users — 12,000 users)

**Target:** Broader mix of plan types, including annual contracts and users with active discounts/credits, but still excluding highest-revenue enterprise accounts and any account currently in a billing dispute.

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completed in full with invoice-accuracy discrepancy rate at or below 0.1% and zero P1/P2 support incidents attributable to migration; support team has confirmed runbook coverage for the top 10 issue types seen in Phase 1.

**Duration:** 3–4 weeks, migrated in weekly sub-batches (e.g., four batches of ~3,000) to keep support load manageable.

**Activities:** New system becomes source of truth for migrated users (customer-facing invoices now generated by new system). Old system retained in read-only/standby mode for these users for at least 30 days post-migration to support rollback and historical lookups.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability / Full Migration (65% of users — 26,000 users)

**Target:** All remaining users, including enterprise, high-complexity, and disputed accounts, migrated last and with individualized review for the highest-revenue accounts.

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 completed with invoice-accuracy discrepancy rate at or below 0.1%, payment failure rate for migrated users within 0.2 percentage points of the old system's baseline, and finance sign-off on reconciliation of Phase 2 revenue totals.

**Duration:** 4–6 weeks, in batches, with enterprise/high-complexity accounts migrated in the final, smallest, most closely monitored batch.

**Activities:** Complete migration of remaining users. **Note:** decommissioning, disabling, or deleting the old billing system is explicitly NOT part of Phase 3 or any migration phase — it is a distinct follow-on phase (a future "Phase 4: Legacy Decommission") gated on its own separate entry criteria (e.g., minimum 60–90 day parallel-run/rollback window elapsed after the last user batch, full data archival completed, and audit/compliance sign-off), to be planned and approved separately after migration is confirmed stable.

---

## Halt / Rollback Metrics

- **Invoice discrepancy rate > 0.5%** (mismatches between old and new system calculated amounts for the same billing period, sampled daily) → halt rollout, freeze further migrations, and investigate before resuming.
- Additional guardrails: payment failure rate increase of more than 1 percentage point over baseline, or any single data-integrity incident affecting more than 50 accounts, also triggers an immediate halt pending review.

---

## Risks

RISK: Proration and credit balances calculated incorrectly during migration, causing over- or under-billing | Run shadow-mode dual invoicing for every account for at least one full billing cycle before cutover, with automated diffing and manual finance review of flagged accounts | Finance Systems Lead
RISK: Payment method tokens fail to transfer correctly to the new processor integration, causing failed charges | Validate token migration in a staging environment with production-like payment gateway sandbox, and pre-validate a sample of tokens for each batch before migrating it | Payments Engineering Lead
RISK: Customer support is overwhelmed by billing-related tickets during high-volume batches, delaying resolution and increasing churn | Stagger batch sizes, pre-brief support with per-phase runbooks, and staff additional on-call support capacity during each migration window | Customer Support Manager
RISK: Rollback of a migrated batch is attempted but data written only to the new system (e.g., new invoices, new payment attempts) is lost or unsynced back to the old system | Maintain a change log/event stream for every migrated account and build a tested reverse-sync procedure before Phase 1 begins | Platform Engineering Lead
RISK: Regulatory/compliance requirements (e.g., tax calculation, invoice retention) are not fully replicated in the new system, creating audit exposure | Complete a compliance parity checklist and obtain legal/compliance sign-off before any customer-facing cutover in Phase 2 | Compliance Officer

PHASES: 3
